title: Single-source shortest paths

problem.name: Single-source shortest paths
problem.statement_latex:
Given a directed graph with nonnegative edge lengths and a source $s$, output $d(v)=\min_{P:s\leadsto v}\sum_{e\in P}w(e)$ for all vertices, together with optional predecessor edges. Unreachable vertices receive distance $+\infty$.
The oracle comparison counts weighted adjacency queries; explicit-input times use the comparison-addition model, with bit or gate costs depending on weight precision.
problem.statement_text: Given a directed graph with nonnegative edge lengths and a source $s$, output $d(v)=\min_{P:s\leadsto v}\sum_{e\in P}w(e)$ for all vertices, together with optional predecessor edges. quantum.headline_latex: $O(n^{3/2}\log^2 n)$ matrix queries or $O(\sqrt{nm}\log^2 n)$ array queries, quantum shortest-path search.
quantum.details_latex: The corresponding lower bounds are $\Omega(n^{3/2})$ and $\Omega(\sqrt{nm})$. The algorithms return all distances and can retain predecessor edges. Their computational overhead includes arithmetic on distances and reversible evaluation of the weighted graph oracle.
quantum.headline_text: $O(n^{3/2}\log^2 n)$ matrix queries or $O(\sqrt{nm}\log^2 n)$ array queries, quantum shortest-path search.

classical.details_latex: The deterministic 2025 algorithm treats directed nonnegative real weights in the comparison-addition model. Taking its minimum with Dijkstra using Fibonacci heaps, $O(m+n\log n)$, gives a useful bound across graph densities. For matrix-oracle input, the tight classical query complexity remains quadratic, so the dense oracle comparison is $n^2$ versus $\widetilde O(n^{3/2})$. Weight precision determines the bit complexity of additions and comparisons.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial oracle speedup, originating in amplitude amplification and minimum finding. The explicit sparse-graph comparison uses the smaller of the two stated classical time bounds.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous query separation, with quantum lower bounds matching the main powers of $n$ and $m$.

hardware.description_latex: Fault tolerance is required for long coherent searches. Active registers use $O(\log n+b)$ logical qubits for $b$-bit distance arithmetic, plus reversible arithmetic and oracle workspace; classical distance records occupy $O(n(\log n+b))$ bits.
